name: Recreation and Parks Commission Liaison Committee Meeting Agenda
minutes_text:
CITY OF BEVERLY HILLS
  455 North Rexford Drive
  Beverly Hills, CA 90210
  Video Teleconference
  Beverly Hills City Council Liaison / Recreation and Parks Commission Committee
  Meeting

  SPECIAL MEETING HIGHLIGHTS

  Monday, June 3, 2024
  2:00 PM

MEETING CALLED TO ORDER
Date / Time:  June 3, 2024 / 2:00 PM
IN ATTENDANCE:  Councilmember John Mirisch, Councilmember Mary Wells, City Manager
  Nancy Coffey, Director of Community Services Stephanie Harris, City
  Architect Mandana Motahari, Community Services Manager Joana Torres,
  Recreation and Parks Commission Chair Amy Sherry

  1) Public Comment:
  a. Terry Austin: She has had artificial turf for 15 years and states that it gets very hot
  in the summer, and in order to use the yard at all, they have to put up pop-up tents
  in order for dogs to use the turf at all. Turf also retains more microbes than DG and
  is harder to keep clean. She also thinks that it is important for the poles of the
  shade structure to be flush with the wall. She also agrees with the concerns of
  using WoofFiber. She also thinks that if the park was better advertised more people
  would use it.

  2) Beverly Hills Community Dog Park - Shade Structure:
  a. Presentation by Mandana Motahari:
  i. The shade structure is necessary due to the oak trees at the dog park not
  being mature enough to provide shade on their own.
  ii. The proposed structures are suspended shade canopies with an aluminum
  frame with multiple panels of textiline shade fabrics with voids in-between
  to allow sunlight to go through.
  iii. The panels are between 6’ to 8’ wide and between 12’ and 16’ long.
  b. The Commission is in support of the shade structures.
  c. The rough estimate for the cost of the structure would be $400,000.
  d. Councilmember Wells would like to get a cost estimate before moving forward with
  the project but otherwise likes the design of the structure.
  e. She also wonders if it is even necessary given how recent respondents to a survey
  of the dog park did not mark shade as a major concern.
  f. Councilmember Mirisch concurred with Councilmember Wells’ concerns.

  3) Beverly Hills Community Dop Park - Ground Covering
  a. City staff, in coordination with the committee, drafted an eight-question survey that
  was posted at the dog park, the Amanda Foundation, all community services social
 Highlights for June 3, 2024
Recreation and Parks Commission Committee

  media sites, and emailed to all 1,941 dog park patrons. The survey ran from
  February 18th to March 10th.
  b. 137 people responded to the survey.
  c. Results were as follows:
  i. 58% of respondents use the park sporadically while 18% use it between 3
  and 5 times a week.
  ii. 45% of respondents identified cleanliness as the number one factor in
  having a successful dog park, while ground covering was at 14% and
  having separate large and small dog areas was at 10%.
  iii. 35% of respondents identified the ground covering as an issue at the dog
  park while 22% had no issues with the park.
  d. The commission explored two alternative ground coverings, WoofFiber and
  K9Grass.
  e. WoofFiber is made from virgin wood fibers, withstands both low and high
  temperatures and reduces mud puddles, craters, dust, and dirt. It is currently used
  at a community residency dog park in Palm Springs. It would cost $26,701.58 to
  procure the material, surface preparation and installation costs are not factored in.
  f. K9Grass is specifically designed for dogs. It has good drainage, built in
  antimicrobial technology, and a dense blade construction which makes it easy to
  locate and remove solid waste. It is currently used at West Hollywood and Signal
  Hill Dog Parks. It would cost between $288,000 and $432,000 to procure and
  install this material depending on the blade density and color selected., surface
  preparation costs are not factored in.
  g. The total costs for the park were around $865,000 to $1,000,000 when it was built.
  h. The active number of users of the dog park is around 400 people.
  i. Councilmember Wells wonders if it is the ground covering or the registration
  requirement that is depressing attendance compared to West Hollywood.
  j. The registration requirement was put in place to make sure that all dogs were up
  to date with their vaccinations and registered with the county.
  k. Artificial turf gets quite hot during the summer.
  l. Additional research is necessary for WoofFiber as there is a concern of dogs eating
  it.
  m. There are no legal barriers to installing artificial turf at the dog park.
  n. The main concerns with the artificial turf at West Hollywood Dog Park is the smell
  and having to close down the park for a few hours to make sure that the cleaning
  products have fully drained from the turf.
  o. Most complaints about the DG are due to dust.
  p. Both Liaisons are in favor of doing a test area with the potential new material prior
  to a full replacement of the DG ground cover.
  q. The liaisons have directed staff to do a full cost estimate of the shade structure as
  well as research for the ground covering including options for the test site,
  modifications to the park rules, as well as costs associated with the replacement.

  4) Adjournment:
  Date / Time: June 3, 2024 / 2:43 PM
